finding.claim: dropTable ignores the error returned by Authorize, so the authorization check is not enforced. Any caller can run DROP TABLE with an attacker-chosen table name. The 't' parameter is also concatenated into the SQL string, which allows SQL injection.
finding.source: HTTP request to /admin/drop: form value 't' (r.FormValue). The caller is any user who reaches the handler, including one without the 'dba' role.

trace.note: /admin/drop is registered with http.HandleFunc and no auth middleware
userFrom(r) loads the user from the context
Authorize(u, "dba") returns an error for non-dba users, but the return value is discarded
r.FormValue("t") is concatenated into the DROP TABLE statement and passed to runSQL

finding.guards_checked: Authorize is called but its error is not checked, unlike in vacuum at api.go:33-36, where it is enforced. There is no middleware on the route, since main uses the default mux directly. There is no allowlist or identifier validation on 't'. runSQL is a stub, but it is the SQL sink. userFrom does an unchecked type assertion, which would panic if no user is in the context, so an unauthenticated request might crash the handler rather than bypass it. That depends on upstream middleware that is not present in this repo.

verdict.guard_found: Authorize(u,"dba") at api.go:26 is called but its error return is discarded; no middleware (api.go:44 uses the default mux directly); no allowlist or validation on 't'. userFrom (api.go:22) does an unchecked type assertion, which only causes a panic when no user is in the context.
verdict.reason: api.go:26 calls Authorize as a bare statement and drops its error, so api.go:27 runs "DROP TABLE "+r.FormValue("t") for any caller who reaches the route (api.go:44); the enforced check in vacuum at api.go:33-36 shows the intended behavior.
